newsitem.title: EGYPT: Jordan's prime minister in Cairo for peace talks.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's prime minister in Cairo for peace talks.

text.p: Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti met Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Wednesday for talks on the deadlocked Middle East peace process.
Kabariti is expected to brief Mubarak on King Hussein's visit to the Palestinian self-rule areas on Tuesday and the monarch's discussions with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
Palestinian officials have said that Hussein was trying to arrange a meeting between the two of them and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The king became the first Arab head of state to visit the self-rule areas and in a joint news conference with Arafat said Jordan, Israel's closest Arab ally, wanted speedy implementation of the peace deals signed with the Palestinians.
Egypt and Jordan are the only two Arab states which have signed peace treaties with Israel.
For almost two weeks, Israeli and Palestinian negotiators have been trying to break an impasse on a long-delayed Israeli troop pullout of the West Bank town of Hebron.
Arafat will also hold talks with Mubarak later on Wednesday.
